title: My BTC bot shorted at 78.6k, sat through the pump to 81k, and closed green on today’s dump — 55/0 so far
author: bytecrawl
selftext:
Sharing an update on the BTC bot I’ve been building.

Yesterday it opened a short at **$78,601**. BTC then ripped toward \~$81k, so the position was about 3.3% underwater at its worst. The bot didn’t panic-close. It kept to its plan, and when BTC dumped today it closed at **$78,443** for **+$377**.

Overall numbers since I started (31+ trading days):

* Starting balance $10k → **$23,945** (+$13,945 net)
* **55 trades, 55 wins, 0 losses, 0 liquidations**
* 415 signals were skipped by its filters. It’s choosy about entries.

I know a 100% win rate looks suspicious, so here’s how I see it: most trades are short holds with small targets, and some (like this one) take real drawdown before they resolve. I’m watching that risk closely. It’s going to lose eventually, and I’d rather understand *how* it loses than pretend it won’t.

Happy to answer questions about the logic. I’d especially like to hear from people. If anyone wants to try it out, DM me and I can get you connected. I’m keeping it to a small group for now so I can watch how it behaves across more accounts and market conditions.

comments.author: bacbac870
comments.body: But it went straight to 76k .. why your bot closed the deal fast .. it was one hour trade

replies.author: bytecrawl
replies.body: It wasn’t a one-hour trade. It shorted yesterday at 78.6k and held about 24h, through the pump to 81k. The bot takes a fixed profit and exits, so it doesn’t try to catch the full drop.

replies.body: Does it have a stop loss? because it sounds like you basically just got lucky. We're in a bear market so shorting paid dividends. What would happen in a bull market? At what point would it have sold?

replies.author: bytecrawl
replies.body: No browser tab. The bot reads price data, places orders and manages exits through that.

comments.author: swifthalf
comments.body: Out of the 415 skipped, 412 would’ve won. Am I reading that correctly? Why is it skipping those when they’re 97% winners? Where are you trading these positions?

replies.author: bytecrawl
replies.body: Yes, you’re reading it right. Most skips happen because a trade is already open. The bot runs one position at a time to keep risk controlled
